answer: A concrete defense is fee-bonded admission with staggered reputation decay. Every agent deposits a bond before acting, and new entrants earn influence slowly, like water filling a lagoon behind a dam, not all at once. A falcon-style watchdog process audits identity clusters: if many accounts behave in lockstep, their bonds are slashed and burned. Routing trust through time-separated checkpoints forms a canyon path that is cheap to walk down but expensive to fake, so mass-creating fake agents loses money instead of gaining voting power.
